⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Continuous-Flow Catalytic Upgrading of Bio-Oils: A Synthetic Long-Form Example

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Introduction

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The reactor was operated at 280 °C for 6 hours under a constant flow of 2.5 mL/min.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Conversion reached 9% after 12 cycles, and the selectivity remained above 89%.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩We attribute the decline to surface fouling, which was confirmed by SEM imaging.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Methods

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The catalyst loading was 40 mg per gram of support, following the protocol of [1].

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Figure 1 summarizes the pressure drop across the bed as a function of time.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩No significant deactivation was observed below 280 °C (p = 0.06).

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The apparent activation energy is 45 kJ/mol, consistent with earlier reports [2, 3].

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Table 1 lists the textural properties of the three prepared samples.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Results and Discussion

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Error bars denote one standard deviation from three independent runs (n = 3).

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The model reproduces the data with a root-mean-square error of 0.10.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩We note that the observed trend may reflect mass-transfer limitations at high flow.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Blank experiments showed no measurable conversion under identical conditions.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The pore size distribution was centered near 8 nm for the calcined sample.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Figure 1. Pressure drop and conversion as functions of time on stream.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Reproducibility across batches was within ±24%.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Long-term stability tests extended to 42 hours without measurable loss.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The reactor was operated at 280 °C for 48 hours under a constant flow of 10.0 mL/min.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Conversion reached 12% after 6 cycles, and the selectivity remained above 89%.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩Conclusion

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩We attribute the decline to surface fouling, which was confirmed by SEM imaging.

⟨SYNTH-ZH⟩The catalyst loading was 35 mg per gram of support, following the protocol of [1].
